etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English mellifluous, mellyfluous, from Latin mellifluus (“flowing like honey”) + -ous, from mel (“honey”) + fluō (“flow”). Compare superfluous and fluid, from same root, and with dulcet (“sweet speech”), alternative Latinate term with a similar meaning. By surface analysis, melli- +‎ -fluous.
senses: (figurative) Sweet, smooth and musical; pleasant to hear (generally used of a person's voice, tone or writing style).
